metaTitle: Kando: learn a language from videos in that language
metaDescription: Kando is a free, open-source desktop app that plays videos with bilingual subtitles: it transcribes the speech on your computer and translates every line.
metaImageAlt: Kando's library: the film finished last, the jobs in progress and the films of the library
heroTitle:
Real videos,
understood line by line.
heroLead: Paste a YouTube or Bilibili link. Kando transcribes the speech on your computer, translates it line by line, and plays the video with the original and the translation on screen together.
heroMeta: Free and open source · MIT license · macOS, Linux, Windows · v{version}
shotPlayerAlt: The player with bilingual subtitles, and every line of the film in the side panel
sitesLead: Works with the {count} websites yt-dlp downloads from: paste a link and go
sitesStripLabel: Some of the websites Kando downloads videos from
stepsEyebrow: From a link to bilingual subtitles
stepDownloadBody: Paste a link or drop in a file. For a site you need to sign in to, sign in once in the built-in browser first.
stepTranscribeBody: The speech is recognized on your own computer, and Kando works out which language is spoken.
stepTranslateBody: Every line is translated into your language, and the model can read the lines before it for context.
stepExportBody: Two subtitle files, the original and a bilingual one, ready to watch and learn from.
libraryTitle:
Everything you're learning from,
in one place
libraryBody: A library is a `.kando` folder of ordinary files. Keep several and switch between them in the sidebar, or filter by YouTube, Bilibili, other websites and files on your computer.
libraryPoint1: Every film gets an original and a bilingual SRT beside it
libraryPoint2: Videos on your computer are transcribed where they are, never copied
libraryPoint3: Every film picks up where you stopped
shotLibraryAlt: The library: the film finished last, the jobs in progress and the films of the library
cliTitle:
Kando for your terminal
and your AI assistant
cliBody: Kando is also the command-line tool `kando` and, with `kando mcp`, an MCP server. Scripts and AI assistants such as Claude can add videos, follow the jobs and read the subtitles.
cliPoint1: {commands} commands: add, list, subtitles, jobs, retry and more, all with --json
cliPoint2: {tools} MCP tools, so an AI assistant can add videos, read subtitles and manage jobs
cliPoint3: When Kando isn't open, a command starts it in the background

cliCommentList: List the library's films from one website

cliCommentStatus: Can a job start, and is anything missing?

detailReplayBody: Jump to the previous or next line, hear this one again, or loop it until you've got it.
detailModesBody: Bilingual, original only, translation only or off. Shift them by 0.1 seconds and change their style.
detailSearchBody: The side panel lists every line; click one to jump to it. It also cuts the film into 4 to 12 clips.
detailWhisperBody: From Tiny (77.7 MB) to Large v3 (3.1 GB): pick the one your computer runs well.
detailAIBody: EveryAPI by default, or OpenAI, DeepSeek, Qwen, Kimi, Ollama and any other OpenAI-compatible API.
detailBrowserBody: Sign in to a website in Browse, and downloads from the link bar, the command line or MCP all use that sign-in.
detailUploadBody: Optional: upload the video and its bilingual subtitles to R2, S3, Alibaba Cloud OSS or Tencent Cloud COS.
detailShortcutsBody: Playback, subtitles and windows all have shortcuts. ⌘/ shows them all; ⌘K opens the command palette.
detailLanguagesBody: 简体中文, 繁體中文, English, 日本語 and 한국어, switched at any time.
openTitle: Free, with all the code on GitHub
openBody: Written in Go with a native interface, no web view. macOS and Linux have ready-made packages; on Windows, build it from source, which makes an installer. Kando updates itself when a new version comes out.
dlMacBody: Download the arm64 .dmg for a Mac with Apple silicon or the amd64 one for an Intel Mac, open it and drag Kando to Applications. It's signed and notarized by Apple.
dlFirstRun: The first time Kando opens, it downloads whichever of yt-dlp, ffmpeg and whisper.cpp are missing.

faqPriceA: Kando is free and open source under the MIT license. Translation uses an AI service, which charges as that provider does; with Ollama or LM Studio the model runs on your own computer.
faqSitesQ: Which websites does it work with?
faqSitesA: YouTube, Bilibili and the other websites yt-dlp downloads from, {count} in all; Help › Supported Websites… in the app lists them. You can also drop mp4, mov, mkv, webm and other files from your computer on the window.
faqSpeechA: On your computer, by whisper.cpp: the audio is never uploaded to be transcribed. A whisper model is downloaded from Hugging Face the first time it's used.
faqTranslateQ: What do I need for translation?
faqTranslateA: Kando translates with EveryAPI by default: sign in once with the EveryAPI CLI (everyapi auth login). Or pick another provider and enter its model and API key in Settings › AI Service; Ollama and LM Studio need no key.
faqSystemsQ: Which systems does it run on?
faqSystemsA: macOS (Apple silicon and Intel) and Linux (x86-64 and ARM64) have ready-made packages. On Windows, build Kando from source for now.
faqLoginQ: What about videos you have to sign in to watch?
faqLoginA: Open the website in Browse in the sidebar and sign in; every download after that uses the sign-in. Clear Sign-in Data… signs you out of them all at once.
faqExportA: Every finished video has two SRT files beside it: the original subtitles, and bilingual ones with the translation above the original, ready for any other player.
